mainTopic: The vegetables used for מרור: which qualify, which is best, why they must be vegetables, and planting them together
overview: The משנה lists five vegetables that can be used for מרור on פסח. They can be fresh or dry, but not pickled or cooked. They combine to make a כזית, the stalk counts, and certain produce with special tithe or holiness status may be used. The גמרא gives the Aramaic name of each vegetable. It then brings ברייתות with longer lists, and three general signs of a bitter herb, with רב הונא ruling like אחרים: it is bitter, has sap, and has a pale surface. A story with רבינא and רב אחא teaches that the preferred מרור is חזרת, lettuce, because it starts soft and ends harsh, like the מצריים. אביי then uses the comparison to מצה to show that מרור must be a vegetable fit for people to eat, and that many kinds qualify. Finally, רב says all the מרור vegetables may be planted in one bed. The גמרא explains that he means planted properly, with spacing, and then begins to challenge that reading from a משנה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The five vegetables for מרור and their acceptable condition
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five vegetables that work for מרור. They may be fresh or dry, but not pickled, over-boiled, or cooked.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the vegetables a person can use to fulfill his obligation on פסח: חזרת, תמכא, חרחבינא, עולשין, and מרור. They work whether fresh or dry, but not if pickled, over-boiled, or cooked.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a list of the five vegetables that can be eaten for the מצוה of מרור. It also explains which states of those vegetables are acceptable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh and dried vegetables are both fine because they still have their bitter taste. Pickling, over-boiling, and cooking take away the plant's natural bitterness, so they no longer count as מרור.

keyTerms.meaning: Bitter herb; here it is also the name of one specific plant
Pickled or soaked (in water or vinegar)

steps.confusionAlert: The word מרור appears twice in this topic. It is the general name of the מצוה (bitter herbs), and it is also the name of one specific plant, the fifth one in this list. Don't mix the two up.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
And these are the vegetables with which a person fulfills
his obligation on Pesach:
with chazeres, with tamcha,
and with charchavina, and with olashin, and with maror.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן בֵּין לַחִין בֵּין יְבֵשִׁין,
phrases.english: One fulfills the obligation with them whether fresh or dry,
phrases.notes: Drying does not remove the bitterness.

phrases.english: but not pickled
and not over-boiled and not cooked.
phrases.notes: These processes take away the bitter taste.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ יְרָקוֹת שֶׁאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five vegetables work for מרור. They are valid fresh or dry, but invalid if pickled, over-boiled, or cooked.

steps.title: Combining the vegetables, using the stalk, and produce with special status
steps.stepSummary: The vegetables can be combined to reach a כזית, and the stalk counts. One may also use דמאי, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken, and redeemed מעשר שני or הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They combine to make a כזית, and one fulfills the obligation with their stalk. One may also use דמאי, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken, and מעשר שני or הקדש that were redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds more practical rules about the amount needed, which part of the plant counts, and which kinds of produce may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You do not need a full כזית from a single vegetable; different types add up together. The listed produce all count because each is now permitted to eat: the needed portion was removed, or the holiness was moved onto money. The גמרא discusses some of these cases later on.

keyTerms.meaning: They combine (to reach a required amount)
An olive-sized amount, the minimum for the מצוה
Produce bought from an unlearned person that may not have been tithed
First tithe, given to a לוי

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives four things: the list of vegetables, the condition they must be in, that they combine to a כזית with the stalk counting, and which kinds of produce are allowed.

phrases.english: And they combine to make an olive-bulk,
and one fulfills the obligation with their stalk.
And with demai produce,
and with first tithe whose terumah has been taken,
phrases.notes: This means the תרומה that the לוי must separate from it.

phrases.english: and second tithe and consecrated property that were redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with more details about the amount, the part of the plant, and the status of the produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The different vegetables combine to a כזית, the stalk counts, and דמאי, מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken, and redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש are all valid.

steps.title: Identifying the five vegetables by their Aramaic names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the everyday name of each vegetable in the משנה. רבה בר בר חנה explains תמכא, and רבי שמעון בן לקיש explains חרחבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: חזרת is חסא (lettuce). עולשין is הינדבי (endive). For תמכא, רבה בר בר חנה said it is called תמכתא. For חרחבינא, רבי שמעון בן לקיש said it is the plant that grows around the palm tree. מרור is מרירתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא translates the Hebrew plant names of the משנה into the Aramaic names people used every day, so we know exactly which plants are meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No law is added here. This is identification, so the reader can find the correct plants. Notice that the order is not the same as in the משנה: עולשין is explained second.

keyTerms.meaning: The first vegetable in the list
Field eryngo, a plant growing around palm trees
The Aramaic name of the plant called מרור

steps.whyThisMatters: Identifying חזרת as lettuce (חסא) is the basis for the common practice of using lettuce for מרור.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Chazeres is chasa (lettuce).
Olashin is hindevi (endive).

phrases.aramaic: תַּמְכָא, אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: Tamcha: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
Its name is temachta.

phrases.aramaic: חַרְחֲבִינָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Charchavina: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
The plant that grows around the palm tree.
And 'with maror': this is merirata.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the plant names listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each vegetable in the משנה is identified by its common Aramaic name.

steps.title: בר קפרא's ברייתא gives a slightly different list
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא teaches a ברייתא listing the vegetables for מרור. It includes a plant not in the משנה: חרחלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: These are the vegetables a person can use to fulfill his obligation on פסח: עולשין, תמכא, חרחלין, חרחבינין, and חזרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with its own list of מרור vegetables, so we can compare it to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats most of the משנה's plants in a different order. It adds חרחלין, and it does not list the plant מרור (מרירתא) by name. This shows that other plants with the same bitter quality can also qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: A bitter plant not listed in the משנה

phrases.english: Bar Kappara teaches:
These are the vegetables with which a person fulfills
his obligation on Pesach:
with olashin, and with tamcha,
with charchalin, with charchavinin, and with chazarin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא whose list differs slightly from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בר קפרא, the valid vegetables are עולשין, תמכא, חרחלין, חרחבינין, and חזרין.

steps.title: רב יהודה adds wild and garden endives
steps.stepSummary: Within the ברייתא, רב יהודה adds that wild endives, garden endives, and חזרת also qualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: Also wild endives, garden endives, and חזרת.
steps.whatsHappening: An additional opinion inside the ברייתא makes the list wider by saying that both wild and garden endives count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה makes clear that עולשין counts whether it grows wild in the field or is grown in a garden. He also mentions חזרת again, even though it already appears on the list. That repetition invites the discussion that comes next in the גמרא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't let the repeated mention of חזרת throw you. It is already on the list, and the גמרא will deal with why it appears again.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says:
Also field endives
and garden endives, and chazeres.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף עוּלְשֵׁי שָׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further opinion to בר קפרא's ברייתא, making the list wider.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both wild and garden עולשין, as well as חזרת, are valid for מרור.

steps.title: Why repeat garden endives and חזרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב יהודה mentions garden endives and חזרת, since the first part of the ברייתא already listed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Garden endives and חזרת? The first part of the ברייתא already taught them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's addition. He seems to repeat plants the ברייתא already listed at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teaching should not repeat itself for no reason. The ברייתא's opening list already included חזרת and עולשין. So why would רב יהודה say them again as if they were something new?

keyTerms.meaning: Garden endives (endives grown in a garden)
But the first part already taught it! (a challenge about repetition)
The first clause or first part of a teaching

phrases.english: Garden endives and chazeret?
phrases.notes: Quoting רב יהודה's addition from Step 5.

phrases.english: But the first clause already taught them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's addition from Step 5 as a repetition.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's inclusion of garden endives and חזרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The opening list of the ברייתא already named these plants, so repeating them seems to add nothing.

steps.title: His real point: wild endives are like garden endives
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's real point is that wild endives are just as good as garden endives and חזרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: even wild endives are like garden endives and חזרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reading רב יהודה more carefully. He is not repeating the list. He is comparing wild endives to the ones already listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Garden endives and חזרת are mentioned only as the standard for comparison. The new information is עולשי שדה, wild endives, which might have seemed different because they grow wild. רב יהודה teaches that they also work.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (re-reading a statement)
Wild endives (endives that grow in a field)

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
even wild endives
are like garden endives and chazeret.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the statement: the repeated items are the point of comparison, not the new addition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה was listing garden endives and חזרת again.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה adds wild endives, comparing them to the plants already listed.

steps.title: רבי מאיר adds more plants
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר adds עסווס, טורא, and מר ירואר to the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: also עסווס, טורא, and מר ירואר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר, still inside the same ברייתא, adds more plants that can be used for מרור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list gets longer. רבי מאיר seems to name three or four separate plants. The next step will question how many plants this really is.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant name (an extra herb for מרור)
A plant name (an extra herb for מרור)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Also asvas, and tura, and mar yero'ar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another addition to the ברייתא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עסווס, טורא, and מר ירואר may also be used for מרור.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: these are the same plants
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says עסווס and טורא are one plant, and מר is the same as ירואר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: עסווס and טורא are one plant, and מר is the same as ירואר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי responds to רבי מאיר. He says the names are doubles: two names for one plant, twice over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי does not say these plants are invalid. He only corrects the count: there are really just two plants, not four. This is about identifying plants, not about the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (a direct reply)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not disagreeing that these plants work for מרור. He only says some of רבי מאיר's names are the same plant.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
Asvas and tura are one plant.
And mar is the same as yero'ar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects רבי מאיר's count of plants in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the counting of separate plants. The validity of the plants is not touched.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי מאיר listed double names for the same plant as if they were separate plants.

steps.title: The school of שמואל's list of vegetables
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of שמואל lists six vegetables that work for מרור on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of שמואל taught: These are the vegetables a person can use to fulfill his obligation on פסח: חזרת, endives, תמכא, חרבינין, חרגינין, and הרדופנין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with its own list of vegetables for מרור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list is close to the משנה's list but uses somewhat different names. It shows another version of the same tradition about which plants count.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of שמואל (a ברייתא from his study hall)
A plant name (a bitter herb on this list)

phrases.english: The school of (Rabbi) Shmuel taught:
These are the vegetables with which a person fulfills
his obligation on Pesach:
With chazeret, with endives, and with chervil,
and with field eryngo, and with charginin, and with hardofanin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא after the ברייתא of בר קפרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six named vegetables may be used for מרור on פסח.

steps.title: רבי יהודה adds two kinds of chazeret
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds חזרת יולין and חזרת גלין, since they are like the listed vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: also חזרת יולין and חזרת גלין, since they are like these vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the school of שמואל's ברייתא, רבי יהודה adds two varieties of חזרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is in the words כיוצא בהן: these plants are similar to the vegetables already listed. So they work too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Also chazeret yolin and chazeret gallin,
as they are similar to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף חֲזֶרֶת יוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the list of Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזרת יולין and חזרת גלין also work for מרור.

steps.title: רבי אילעא: ערקבלים also work
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא reports in the name of רבי אליעזר that ערקבלים may also be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא says in the name of רבי אליעזר: also ערקבלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא adds another plant, ערקבלים, and says he heard it from his teacher רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new addition based on a tradition from a teacher. The next step will show that רבי אילעא needed support for this report.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant name (another herb for מרור)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אִילְעָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ila'a says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
Also arkablim,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אִילְעָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another addition to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערקבלים may also be used for מרור.

steps.title: רבי אילעא finds support for his report
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא searched among רבי אליעזר's students for someone to back him up and found no one. Then רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agreed with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: I went around to all his students looking for a colleague who agreed, and I did not find one. But when I came before רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, he agreed with my words.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא tells how he tried to confirm his tradition. At first no one remembered it, but later רבי אליעזר בן יעקב agreed with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A report heard by only one student could be doubted. רבי אילעא's ruling stood alone until a respected sage, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, agreed. That agreement supports his addition of ערקבלים.

keyTerms.meaning: A colleague (someone to agree with me)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is a different person from רבי אליעזר, whose statement רבי אילעא is reporting.

phrases.english: And I went around to all his students
and I looked for a colleague, but I did not find one.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁבָּאתִי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: And when I came before Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
he agreed with my words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives support for רבי אילעא's report in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The addition of ערקבלים reported in the name of רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreement of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: רבי יהודה: any plant with sap
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives a general sign: any plant that has sap may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: any plant that has sap.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now moves from listing plants to giving a general sign. רבי יהודה says any plant with sap works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of naming each plant, רבי יהודה gives one test. If the plant has sap (שרף), usually a white liquid when cut, it qualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: Sap (a liquid, usually white, that comes out when the plant is cut)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Any plant that has sap.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שָׂרָף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from naming plants to a general sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any plant with sap qualifies for מרור.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: a pale surface
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה gives a different sign: any plant whose surface is pale.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: any plant whose surface is pale.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different general sign. He looks at the plant's color instead of its sap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, the test is that the leaf surface is pale or light green (פנים מכסיפין). He does not mention sap.

keyTerms.meaning: Its surface is pale or light green

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
Anything whose surface is pale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different sign from רבי יהודה's in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any plant with a pale surface qualifies for מרור.

steps.title: אחרים: a bitter herb with both signs
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say a valid plant is a bitter vegetable that has sap and a pale surface.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: any bitter vegetable that has sap and whose surface is pale.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view combines the earlier signs. The plant must be bitter, have sap, and have a pale surface.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים require more than either earlier view. One sign alone is not enough. The plant needs both signs, and it must also be bitter.

keyTerms.meaning: "Others" (an unnamed תנא or group of תנאים)

phrases.english: Acheirim say:
[Any] bitter vegetable
that has sap and whose surface is pale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two signs of Steps 14 and 15 and adds bitterness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A valid herb must be bitter, have sap, and have a pale surface.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: learn from all of them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that from all these opinions together we learn: a bitter vegetable has sap and a pale surface.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: From the words of all of them we learn that a bitter vegetable has sap and its surface is pale.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן puts the opinions together. He draws one combined picture of what a true bitter herb looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא gave one sign. רבי יוחנן reads them together: a real bitter herb has both sap and a pale surface. This matches the view of אחרים.

keyTerms.meaning: From the words of all of them we learn

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
From the words of all of them we learn
that a bitter vegetable has sap
and its surface is pale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the opinions of Steps 14 to 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A true bitter herb has both sap and a pale surface.

steps.title: רב הונא: the הלכה follows אחרים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the הלכה follows אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The הלכה follows אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the final ruling. The הלכה follows אחרים, who require bitterness, sap, and a pale surface.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among the three general signs, the ruling goes with the strictest, combined view. A plant used for מרור needs all of these features.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא lists many plants for מרור and then gives general signs. The final ruling, from רב הונא, follows אחרים: a valid herb is bitter, has sap (שרף), and has a pale surface (פנים מכסיפין).
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical test for recognizing a proper bitter herb, beyond the specific names in the lists.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The halacha is like Acheirim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after רבי יוחנן's summary.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows אחרים: a valid מרור is bitter, has sap, and has a pale surface.

steps.title: רבינא finds רב אחא searching for a very bitter herb
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: רב אחא בריה דרבא is going out of his way to find מרירתא for מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא found רב אחא the son of רבא searching for מרירתא, a very bitter herb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a short story. This line only sets the scene for the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא listed several plants that may be used for מרור. Here we see a real person picking one of them on purpose. We are about to find out whether his choice is the best one.

keyTerms.meaning: Searching for, going out of his way to get
A very bitter herb, one of the kinds of מרור

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
phrases.english: Ravina found Rav Acha, son of Rava,
who was searching for merirata (a very bitter herb).
phrases.notes: He wanted this specific herb for מרור.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rules about which plants count as מרור, the גמרא tells a story about which plant is the best choice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רב אחא preferred מרירתא, the most bitter herb.

steps.title: רבינא shows that the sources prefer lettuce
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks why he wants the most bitter herb, when the משנה and other sources put חזרת first, and חזרת is lettuce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: What are you thinking? That it is better because it is more bitter? But we learned חזרת first in the משנה. The school of שמואל also taught חזרת first. רבי אושעיא said the best way to do the מצוה is with חזרת. And רבא said that חזרת means חסא, lettuce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אחא's choice. He brings four sources showing that the preferred מרור is חזרת, which is lettuce, and not the most bitter herb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא seems to think that more bitter means a better מרור. רבינא pushes back with a chain of sources. The משנה lists חזרת first. The school of שמואל also lists it first. רבי אושעיא says outright that the מצוה is best done with it. Finally, רבא identifies חזרת as lettuce.

keyTerms.meaning: The first kind of מרור listed in the משנה
The best way to do the מצוה is with חזרת

steps.confusionAlert: Many people think חזרת means horseradish. Here the גמרא says clearly that חזרת is חסא, lettuce.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your thinking?
That they are more bitter?
But we learned chazeret (first in the Mishnah)!
And the school of Shmuel taught: chazeret (first),
and Rabbi Oshaya said: The best way to do the מצוה is with chazeret.
And Rava said: What is chazeret? Lettuce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ, דִּמְרִירִין טְפֵי? וְהָא חֲזֶרֶת תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אחא's choice of herb from the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא's view that the most bitter herb is the best מרור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה, the school of שמואל, and רבי אושעיא all put חזרת first or call it the best choice, and רבא identifies it as lettuce. So being more bitter does not make an herb the preferred one.

steps.title: The name lettuce hints at God's mercy
steps.stepSummary: The word חסא is explained as a hint to the fact that God had mercy on us.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it called חסא? Because the Merciful One had mercy (חס) on us.
steps.whatsHappening: The argument for lettuce continues. The name חסא itself carries a message that fits the סדר night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חסא sounds like חס, which means having mercy. So lettuce fits the theme of the night especially well: God took pity on us and redeemed us. This adds a reason beyond the sources for why lettuce is preferred.

phrases.english: What is 'chassa'? That the Merciful One had mercy (chas) on us.
phrases.notes: A play on the sound of the word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a reason, based on the name, for preferring lettuce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The name חסא hints at God's mercy, חס.

steps.title: Egypt was like lettuce: soft at first, harsh at the end
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains that the מצריים are compared to מרור because they started out soft and ended up harsh, just like this מרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Why are the מצריים compared to מרור? To teach you that this מרור starts soft and ends hard, and so too the מצריים started soft and ended hard.
steps.whatsHappening: A second support for lettuce. The way lettuce behaves matches the story of Egypt, which is what מרור is meant to remind us of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lettuce is mild at first and turns bitter and hard as it grows. This matches the מצריים, who were friendly at first and then harsh. Herbs that are bitter from the very start do not show this change, so lettuce fits the message of מרור best.

keyTerms.meaning: Its end is hard or harsh

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the best מרור is not chosen for sharpness alone. It is the plant that best tells the story of slavery in Egypt.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yonatan:
Why are the Egyptians compared to maror?
To tell you: just as this maror
is soft at the start and hard at the end,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִצְרִיִּים תְּחִילָּתָן רַכָּה וְסוֹפָן קָשָׁה.
phrases.english: so too the Egyptians were soft at the start and harsh at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reason for preferring lettuce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן's comparison: the מצריים were soft at first and harsh at the end, just like lettuce.

steps.title: רב אחא takes back his view
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא accepts the arguments and agrees that lettuce is the better choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I take back what I thought.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא is convinced and changes his mind. This ends the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources and reasons from רבינא win the argument. The conclusion is that חזרת, lettuce, is the preferred מרור, even though other herbs are more bitter.

keyTerms.meaning: I take it back, I change my mind

steps.whatToRemember: The best מרור is חזרת, which is lettuce. This is because the sources list it first, its name hints at God's mercy, and it starts soft and ends harsh like the מצריים. Being the most bitter does not make an herb the best choice.

phrases.english: He said to him: I retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אחא accepts the challenge and the reasons that supported it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חזרת, lettuce, is the preferred מרור.

steps.title: How do we know מרור must be a vegetable?
steps.stepSummary: רב רחומי asks אביי how we know מרור is a vegetable. Maybe it could be something bitter like fish bile.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב רחומי said to אביי: How do we know that this מרור is a kind of vegetable? Maybe it means the bitter bile of the כופיא fish?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רב רחומי asks for the source that מרור must be a plant at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מרור only means something bitter. Fish bile is extremely bitter, so why not use it? רב רחומי wants to know what limits מרור to plants.

keyTerms.meaning: The bile of the כופיא fish

phrases.english: Rav Rechumi said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּאי דְּהַאי מָרוֹר מִין יָרָק הוּא?
phrases.english: From where do we know that this maror is a kind of vegetable?
Maybe say it is the bile of the kufya fish?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּהַאי מָרוֹר מִין יָרָק הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from which vegetable is best to asking why מרור must be a vegetable at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that מרור must be a plant and cannot be any bitter thing, such as fish bile.

steps.title: Like מצה, מרור must grow from the ground
steps.stepSummary: מרור is compared to מצה. מצה grows from the ground, so מרור must also grow from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like מצה: just as מצה comes from things that grow from the ground, so too מרור must come from things that grow from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by comparing מרור to מצה, since the פסוק mentions them together. This rules out fish bile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to eat the קרבן פסח with מצה and מרור, so the two are linked. מצה is made from grain, which grows in the ground. So מרור must also be something that grows from the ground, and fish bile does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that grow from the ground

phrases.english: It is similar to matzah:
just as matzah is something that grows from the ground,
so too maror is something that grows from the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּמְיָא דְּמַצָּה: מָה מַצָּה גִּידּוּלֵי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב רחומי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מרור is compared to מצה, so it must grow from the ground. This rules out fish bile.

steps.title: Maybe the bitter oleander shrub?
steps.stepSummary: The הירדוף, a bitter shrub, also grows from the ground. Maybe it could be מרור?
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say it is הירדוף, the bitter oleander shrub?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Growing from the ground is not enough, because the bitter shrub הירדוף also grows from the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first comparison only rules out things that do not grow from the ground. הירדוף is a woody plant that does grow in the ground and is bitter. So the rule needs to be made narrower.

phrases.english: But maybe say oleander?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 25 as too broad.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that anything that grows from the ground can be מרור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הירדוף grows from the ground and is bitter, but it is a shrub, not a vegetable.

steps.title: Like מצה, מרור must be a seed plant, not a tree
steps.stepSummary: מצה comes from a seed plant, so מרור must also come from a seed plant. This rules out a shrub like הירדוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like מצה: just as מצה is from a kind of seed plant, so too מרור must be from a kind of seed plant.
steps.whatsHappening: The same comparison to מצה is made more precise. This rules out the oleander shrub.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain is a plant grown from seeds, not a tree. So מרור must also be a seed plant like a vegetable. A woody shrub such as הירדוף does not qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of seed plant, meaning a plant and not a tree

phrases.english: It is similar to matzah:
just as matzah is a kind of seed plant,
so too maror is a kind of seed plant.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּמְיָא דְּמַצָּה: מָה מַצָּה מִין זְרָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הירדוף challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Makes the comparison to מצה more precise.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any bitter thing that grows from the ground, even a shrub, could be מרור.
steps.terutzMaskana: מרור must be a seed plant, like the grain used for מצה.

steps.title: Maybe the poisonous הרזיפו plant?
steps.stepSummary: הרזיפו is a seed plant, but it is poisonous. Maybe it could be מרור?
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say it is הרזיפו, a plant that poisons animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again. Being a seed plant is still not enough, because הרזיפו is a seed plant but it is poisonous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הרזיפו passes both earlier tests: it grows from the ground and it is a seed plant. But it is harmful to eat. The rule needs one more limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A poisonous plant that is not fit to eat

phrases.english: But maybe say harzipu (a poisonous plant)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 27 as still too broad.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that any seed plant can be מרור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הרזיפו is a seed plant, but it is poisonous and not food.

steps.title: Like מצה, מרור must be food you can buy with מעשר money
steps.stepSummary: מצה can be bought with כסף מעשר שני, so מרור must also be something you can buy with that money. This means it must be human food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like מצה: just as מצה is something you can buy with מעשר money, so too מרור must be something you can buy with מעשר money.
steps.whatsHappening: The comparison to מצה is made more precise a third time. This rules out the poisonous plant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money from מעשר שני may only be spent on food that people eat. מצה qualifies, so מרור must also be real human food. A poisonous plant like הרזיפו is not.

keyTerms.meaning: מעשר שני money, which may only be spent on food for people

steps.whatToRemember: Every limit on מרור comes from comparing it to מצה. מרור must grow from the ground, it must be a seed plant and not a tree, and it must be food that people eat, the kind you can buy with מעשר money.

phrases.english: It is similar to matzah:
just as matzah is something that can be bought with tithe money,
so too maror is something that can be bought with tithe money.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּמְיָא דְּמַצָּה: מָה מַצָּה שֶׁנִּיקַּחַת בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הרזיפו challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Makes the comparison to מצה more precise again.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any seed plant, even a poisonous one, could be מרור.
steps.terutzMaskana: מרור must be human food that can be bought with מעשר שני money.

steps.title: Maybe only one vegetable counts for מרור
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנין asks אביי why many vegetables qualify, when maybe מרור means only one specific vegetable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב חנין said to אביי: Say that מרור is just one kind of vegetable!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. רבה בר רב חנין asks אביי: why say many vegetables work for מרור? Maybe the תורה means just one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before used the comparison to מצה to describe what kind of plant מרור is. This challenge asks a different question: how many plants qualify. Maybe the word מרור points to one single bitter vegetable.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / I could say (introduces a suggestion or challenge)
Bitter herb eaten at the סדר

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנִין לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Chanin said to Abaye:
Say that marror is only one kind!
phrases.notes: Meaning only one specific vegetable could be used, not a whole list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what kind of plant מרור is to how many kinds qualify.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that many vegetables can be used for מרור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word מרור could refer to one single vegetable, so there is no reason to allow a list.

steps.title: The פסוק says ״מרורים״ in the plural
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the תורה writes ״מרורים״, a plural word, so more than one kind qualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written ״מרורים״ (bitter herbs, plural).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers: the פסוק says ״מרורים״, which is plural. So it cannot mean only one vegetable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the wording of the פסוק. A plural word shows that more than one kind of bitter vegetable is included.

keyTerms.meaning: Bitter herbs (plural form in the פסוק)

phrases.english: "Bitter herbs" (plural) is written.
phrases.notes: אביי is answering. The פסוק is שמות יב:ח, ״על מצות ומררים יאכלהו״.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual proof from a plural word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מרור could be only one vegetable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural ״מרורים״ shows that more than one kind works.

steps.title: Maybe the plural means only two
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנין pushes further: a plural only proves two kinds, not many.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that ״מרורים″ means two!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב חנין pushes back. A plural word means at least two, so maybe only two vegetables qualify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The smallest plural is two. So the plural word proves more than one, but it does not prove a long list of five vegetables.

phrases.english: But say that "bitter herbs" means two!
phrases.notes: The smallest number a plural can mean is two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the answer of step 31 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the plural ״מרורים״ to allow many vegetables
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plural only proves at least two, not an open number of kinds.

steps.title: Like מצה, מרור comes from many kinds
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers from the comparison to מצה: מצה can be made from many grains, so מרור can come from many vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like מצה. Just as מצה comes from many kinds, so too מרור comes from many kinds.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי goes back to the comparison between מרור and מצה. מצה can be made from several grains, so מרור can come from several vegetables too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same comparison used in steps 25 to 29 now answers the number question. Since מצה is not limited to one or two grains, מרור is not limited to one or two vegetables.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too (a comparison formula)

steps.whatToRemember: Many vegetables count for מרור, both because the פסוק says ״מרורים″ and because מרור is compared to מצה, which comes from many grains.

phrases.english: It is similar to matzah:
just as matzah comes from many kinds,
phrases.notes: מצה can be made from five grains: wheat, barley, spelt, oats, and rye.

phrases.english: so too marror comes from many kinds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32 by using the מצה comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only two vegetables qualify, the smallest plural.
steps.terutzMaskana: Many vegetables qualify, just like the many grains of מצה.

steps.title: All the מרור vegetables may be planted in one bed
steps.stepSummary: רב says all the vegetables that work for מרור may be planted together in a single garden bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב: The vegetables the חכמים said a person can use to fulfill his obligation on פסח may all be planted in one garden bed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. רב says all the vegetables that work for מרור may be planted together in one garden bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from the laws of פסח to the laws of planting. רב is saying something about how these vegetables relate to each other as plants.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said that Rav said:
The vegetables that the Sages said

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: that a person fulfills his obligation with them on Pesach,
phrases.notes: These are the vegetables listed in the משנה for מרור.

phrases.english: may all be planted in one garden bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New statement about the same vegetables, now from the angle of planting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the vegetables used for מרור may be planted in one garden bed.

steps.title: Does this mean they are not כלאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a conclusion from רב: these vegetables must not count as כלאים with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that the law of כלאים does not apply to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב must mean: these vegetables are not כלאים with each other. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally it is forbidden to plant different kinds of plants together. If רב allows all of them in one bed, he must hold they are similar enough to count as one kind. The question mark shows the גמרא is about to test this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say (introduces a conclusion drawn from a statement)
Forbidden mixing of different species, here planting different kinds together

steps.confusionAlert: רב never said the word כלאים. The גמרא is reading this into his words, and that reading is what רבא will attack.

phrases.english: Is that to say that the prohibition of mixed species does not apply to them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a כלאים conclusion from רב's planting statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב means that the מרור vegetables are not כלאים with each other.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה allows only matching pairs
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה that lists pairs of plants that are not כלאים. It implies that different pairs, like חזרת and עולשין, are כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: חזרת and חזרת גלין, endive and wild endive, leek and wild leek, coriander and wild coriander, mustard and Egyptian mustard, Egyptian gourd and רמוצה are not כלאים with each other. So חזרת with חזרת גלין is allowed, but חזרת with endive is not!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב from a משנה in כלאים. The משנה only allows each plant with its matching wild or foreign version, so חזרת and עולשין, both מרור vegetables, would be כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists plants in pairs: a plant and its close relative. That suggests only a plant and its own pair are not כלאים. Since חזרת and עולשין are each from a different pair, planting them together is forbidden, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (usually from a תנאי source)

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
Lettuce and chazeret gallin,
phrases.notes: A wild type of lettuce.

phrases.english: endive and wild endive,
leek and wild leek,
coriander and wild coriander,
mustard and Egyptian mustard,
and Egyptian gourd and ramutzah,
phrases.notes: A type of gourd.

phrases.english: are not mixed species with each other.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in כלאים א:ב.

phrases.english: Lettuce and chazeret gallin, yes, they may be planted together,
but lettuce and endive, no!
phrases.notes: Both are מרור vegetables, yet they would be כלאים, which goes against רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 35 using a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that all מרור vegetables may be planted in one bed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows only matching pairs together, so two different מרור vegetables like חזרת and עולשין are כלאים.

steps.title: Maybe the whole list is one group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a defense: maybe the משנה means all the listed plants may be planted together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that it teaches all of them together...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way to save רב: maybe the משנה's whole list may be planted together, not just in pairs. This is a setup, and the next step knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is one big group, then חזרת and עולשין may be planted together, and רב is fine. The words ״וכי תימא״ show this answer is raised only so it can be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer that will be rejected)

phrases.english: And if you will say
that it teaches all of them together,
phrases.notes: Meaning any plant on the list may be planted with any other.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא כּוּלְּהוּ בַּהֲדָדֵי קָתָנֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a way to save רב from רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה as one combined group
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows only pairs, which contradicts רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe the משנה allows the whole list together, which would fit רב.

steps.title: רב himself said the list is in pairs
steps.stepSummary: The suggested defense fails, because רב himself said the משנה teaches the plants in pairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say: It teaches them in pairs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the defense. רב himself said the משנה is teaching pairs, so he cannot also read it as one big group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's own reading of the משנה is that each plant goes only with its partner. That means חזרת and עולשין are still כלאים by his own words. So the defense fails, and the next step resolves the contradiction by rereading רב's word 'planted.'

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say (introduces a rejection)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling that all מרור vegetables can share one bed seems to clash with his own reading of the משנה in כלאים, which allows only matching pairs.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
It teaches them in pairs!
phrases.notes: Each plant may only be planted with its own partner in the list.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב זוּגוֹת זוּגוֹת קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 37.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the משנה's whole list may be planted together
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב himself read the משנה as pairs, so the defense goes against his own words.

steps.title: רב meant the vegetables are planted the proper way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב: 'planted together' means planted properly, with the required spacing so there is no כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did רב mean by 'they may be planted'? He meant they may be planted according to their rules, meaning with proper spacing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves רב's statement by giving it a new meaning. רב was not saying these vegetables are not כלאים. He was saying they may share one bed if they are spaced out correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 38 showed that רב himself reads the משנה in pairs, so חזרת and עולשין are כלאים with each other. That makes 'all may be planted together' impossible if read literally. The fix is that 'planted' means planted כהלכתן, the halachic way, with separation between the kinds, so no כלאים is violated.

keyTerms.meaning: They may be planted (רב's word from step 34)
According to their rules, the proper halachic way (here: with the required space between kinds)
What? Used here to ask what a word really means

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא now says these vegetables are not כלאים. They ARE כלאים with each other. רב only allows them in one bed with proper spacing.

phrases.english: What is 'they may be planted' that Rav said?
phrases.notes: The גמרא asks for the real meaning of רב's word.

phrases.english: They may be planted according to their rules.
phrases.notes: Meaning: with the spacing that prevents כלאים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 38 rejected the first defense. This step gives a new defense by reinterpreting רב's word 'planted.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב meant the vegetables are not כלאים with each other at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב meant they may be planted in one bed the proper way, with the required spacing between kinds.

steps.title: Planting properly is already taught in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if רב only meant 'planted properly,' we already learned that in a משנה. It then begins to quote that משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Planted properly'? We already learned that in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading as making רב's statement unnecessary. This is a setup line: it opens a quote of a משנה, which comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב only teaches that different vegetables can share a bed with proper spacing, he adds nothing new, because a משנה already says this. An אמורא is not expected to repeat what an explicit משנה already teaches, so the new reading seems pointless. The proof will come from the משנה that the גמרא is about to quote.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned it (in a משנה). This signals that a statement may be repetitive.
According to their rules; the גמרא repeats step 39's word in order to question it

phrases.english: Properly? We already learned it:
phrases.notes: The משנה being quoted comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step attacks the reinterpretation in step 39 as redundant.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רב as 'planted properly, with spacing'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that is all רב meant, an explicit משנה already teaches it, so רב's statement would be unnecessary.
